## 1. Correction to `epm:clarify v1` item 5

That marker states "31 `scripts/issue*_*.py` entrypoints currently reference
`PHASES`". That came from a loose grep and is **wrong**. Anchored on
`^PHASES\b`, the figure is **15**. Separately, the population that actually
matters for an argparse-attribute-completeness check is not the PHASES set at
all — it is the **927** `scripts/issue*_*.py` files carrying any `args.*`
reference. The clarify marker's item 5 should be read as superseded by this
note.

## 2. A strict whole-module check FAILs 83 files as of today

#2163's heuristic (`ap.add_argument("--x")` → defined; `args.y` → referenced;
whole-module scope) applied to all 927 candidates yields **83 FAILs**. At least
**47 of the 83 are provably false positives** in three systematic classes the
regex cannot see, each confirmed against a verbatim source line:

| Class | n | Confirmed evidence |
|-------|---|--------------------|
| explicit `dest=` rename | 23 | `scripts/issue1090_fu6.py:3489` — `p.add_argument("--no-upload", dest="upload", action="store_false", default=True)`; the regex records `no_upload` while the real dest is `upload` |
| `add_subparsers(dest=...)` | 9 | `scripts/issue1090_fu3_worker.py:1148` — `sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)` |
| runtime namespace assignment | 15 | `scripts/issue1092_gpu_phase.py:4198-4199` — `args.phases_set = parse_phase_set(...)`, `args.phase_name = ",".join(...)` |

The residual 36 are not all true positives either: a **fourth** FP class is
visible but unmodelled — a parser built by an IMPORTED helper. Fingerprint:
`verbose` flagged identically across four siblings
(`issue1491_ladder_{contrasts,fits,generate_capture,manifest}.py`), the
signature of a shared `_add_common_args(ap)` in another module rather than four
independent bugs. True-positive count is therefore materially below 36, and the
heuristic's precision on this population is poor — far worse than #2163's
single-file experience implied, because that driver used none of `dest=`,
subparsers, runtime assignment, or a shared builder.

## Consequence for the design fork

**A repo-wide FAIL-posture `workflow_lint.py` check is foreclosed by
measurement, not by taste.** `workflow_lint.py`'s no-flags default run is the
fleet's Step 9c gate, so landing it red across 83 files would wedge every
task's gate until 83 unrelated files were touched — the #1388 shape ("two
inline-landed lint-red scripts broke the Step 9c gate fleet-wide"). The shapes
that survive: (1) a driver-local check invoked from the driver's own
`--import-check` plus a `code-style.md` rule carrying the canonical snippet and
the whole-module-scope rationale — what #2163 actually shipped, blast radius
zero; or (2) a DIFF-SCOPED WARN that only scans files the round touches, with
all four FP classes handled. Any lint form proposed must state the measured
baseline red count and how it reaches zero.

Whatever form layer (b) takes, its tests must cover all four false-positive
classes — a check that flags `dest="upload"` as missing is not shippable.

## The two Must-Fixes

**MF1 (Statistics) — the invariant is self-consistent, not falsifiable.** A marker
declaring `arm-registry: source=sorted(PHASES) file=<path> n=10 members=<the same
10 it enumerates>` passes clause 3 (`n == len(members)`), clause 5 (`members −
per_arm = ∅`) and clause 6, because the checker never opens `file=` (v1 declared
`source`/`file` "opaque provenance tokens"). The #2163 shape — hand-listed
10-of-13 — passes with nothing but a `source=` relabel. That fails the Goal's word
"MECHANICALLY". Fix: a driver-recompute mode on the D2 CLI as the primary
mechanical arm (v1's "the checker cannot see the driver" premise is wrong for the
normal case — the orchestrator holds the worktree path because it just ran the
smoke there), plus a strengthened reviewer set-equality duty as the fallback when
`file=` does not resolve, with marker-only PASSes made visibly distinct from
driver-verified ones.

**MF2 (Methodology) — the rename is statement-incomplete.** v1's A7 sweep
established the correct six-FILE set (independently confirmed by the
fact-checker on both refs), but was file-grain and its `"plan-named arm"` grep
missed the `"planned arm"` variant. Verified census on the landing base
(`origin/issue-2171`): 16 `plan(ned|-named) arm` statements across the six
surfaces, of which the v1 edit set names roughly 6 of ~14 non-exempt ones.
Unnamed: SKILL.md :4517/:4519 (the PASS_UNIFIED and PASS_PARTIAL routing rows —
D5 only inserted a paragraph *after* the table), experiment-implementer.md
:129/:143, workflow.yaml :1594/:1619, experiment-implementer-section-reference.md
:76/:93/:121. Two genuine exemptions verified and to be declared: SKILL.md :3172
(Step 5c-bis example blocker phrasing) and workflow.yaml :2513 (campaign fields).
T3.2 upgrades from token-presence to statement-grain so a future partial rename
is test-breaking. Telling detail: D8(ii) already performed this exact rename in
the section-reference twin at :94 — the plan knew the phrase class needed
renaming and did it in one file but not its sibling.
